The last man out of the Fire and into Paradise keeps asking for more and is granted the world ten times over; Moses asked about Paradise's lowest and highest ranks.
Seventy thousand of the Ummah will enter Paradise without reckoning, faces like the full moon, using no charms, omens or cautery but trusting their Lord; Ukkasha is one of them.
The Prophet hoped his Ummah would be half the people of Paradise, though few as a white hair on a black ox, Gog and Magog being the Fire's thousands.
Allah has prepared for His pious servants what no eye saw, no ear heard and no heart perceived, as the verse says no soul knows what is hidden for them.
In Paradise a rider cannot cross a tree's shade in a hundred years, and Allah tells its people He will grant them His pleasure and never be displeased with them.
Paradise's people will see those in the chambers above them like shining planets on the horizon, and believers who affirm the truth will reach the abodes of the Apostles.
A street of Paradise visited each Friday adds beauty, and the first to enter have faces like the full moon, no bodily waste, musk sweat, gold combs and two wives.
Paradise's people eat and drink without waste, their food passing as belching and musk sweat; they praise Allah as they breathe and are promised lasting health, life, youth and plenty.
A believer in Paradise has a tent of one hollow pearl sixty miles wide; Saihan, Jaihan, Euphrates and Nile are among its rivers, and some enter with hearts like birds'.
